claims.claim: Mobileye purchases all EyeQ SoCs from a single supplier and remains substantially reliant on timely EyeQ shipments from STMicroelectronics and ECU shipments from Quanta; management is adding TSMC for future EyeQ generations and imaging-radar components, which is a resilience path but not yet evidence that current single-source exposure is eliminated.

Q2 2026 revenue was approximately flat year over year despite 3% higher system volumes because lower EyeQ ASP, primarily from higher China OEM mix, offset volume growth; adjusted gross margin also declined as lower-ASP China mix and higher-hardware-content SuperVision mix increased.

OEM sourcing visibility is not equivalent to contracted volume: Mobileye states OEM programs can change in timing and volumes and do not contractually commit OEMs to particular purchase volumes. This is a direct falsifier against treating design-win visibility as guaranteed backlog.

Intel relationship creates both capability and governance dependency: Mobileye identifies access to Intel radar technology as differentiating, while its 2026 10-K states the relevant radar license is limited and additional radar products may require separate Intel licensing. This should be treated as a dependency/optionality tradeoff rather than a present blocker.

causalEdges: AI/automotive semiconductor demand -> component competition/lead times -> EyeQ/ECU availability and cost -> Mobileye delivery capacity -> OEM deployment
China OEM mix -> lower EyeQ ASP -> revenue/gross-margin pressure -> reduced benefit from unit-volume growth
OEM design win/nomination -> expected model inclusion but no contractual volume -> program timing/volume variability -> realized revenue uncertainty
Intel radar IP access -> differentiated radar development capability; limited license scope -> potential future licensing dependency -> substitution/resilience constraint
risks: single/limited supplier exposure for EyeQ and ECUs
design-win visibility may be mistaken for committed backlog
Intel radar-IP licensing dependency for some future radar scope
unknowns: How much current EyeQ production can be shifted away from STMicroelectronics and on what timeline?
Whether lower China ASP is offset by durable unit economics and gross profit per vehicle over a full product cycle.
How much future radar roadmap scope requires additional Intel licensing versus independently controlled IP.
recommendedNextState: council-alpha should source-address missing_score_risk_evidence using these observed downside/falsifier inputs without treating them as a numeric risk score
falsifiers: Current supplier diversification evidence showing meaningful production redundancy would reduce the single-source risk.
Sustained gross-profit expansion despite lower ASP mix would weaken the pricing/mix downside thesis.
Binding OEM volume commitments would invalidate treating a specific program as non-contracted visibility.
Evidence of independently controlled radar IP covering future roadmap needs would reduce Intel licensing dependency.
